groups.title: Axios HTTP Client in Vue
groups.question: Your Vue SPA talks to Laravel with Sanctum cookies, and every component handles 401 errors differently. Explain how you would set up Axios.

followUps.CSRF Token Injection from Laravel Cookie: How does the CSRF token reach Laravel when using Sanctum cookies?

evidence.text: Request interceptors add headers to every outgoing request.
Response interceptors handle errors like 401 and 403 in one place.
A 401 can trigger a single redirect to the login page.
The SPA first calls Sanctum's csrf-cookie endpoint, which sets an XSRF-TOKEN cookie.
Axios reads that cookie and sends it in the X-XSRF-TOKEN header.
Requests must be sent with credentials so the session cookie is included.

notEnough: Only saying you send the CSRF token.

groups.title: State Management with Pinia
groups.question: The cart, current user and notifications are needed across many Vue components. Explain how you would manage this with Pinia.

followUps.Pinia Stores — Actions, Getters, and Sta: How are state, getters and actions organised in a Pinia store?
followUps.Pinia vs Vuex — Why Pinia Wins for Vue 3: Why choose Pinia over Vuex for Vue 3?

evidence.text: State holds the reactive data.
Getters are computed values derived from state.
Actions change state and can call the API.
Pinia has no mutations, so the API is simpler.
It has good TypeScript support.
Stores are separate modules without nesting, and it works with Vue Devtools.

groups.title: Inertia.js for Full-Stack Integration
groups.question: Your team is tired of building and maintaining a separate JSON API just for its own Vue frontend. Explain how Inertia.js changes this.

followUps.Inertia's Page Component Model: How does Inertia let a controller render a Vue page without an API?
followUps.Shared Data and Partial Reloads: What are shared data and partial reloads?

evidence.text: Laravel controllers return Inertia responses naming a Vue page.
Data is passed as props to that page component.
No separate JSON API or client-side fetching is needed for those pages.

notEnough: Only saying Inertia connects Laravel and Vue.

evidence.text: Shared data, like the logged-in user, is added to every page automatically.
Partial reloads request only some props again.
This avoids repeating queries and reloading data that did not change.

groups.title: CORS Configuration
groups.question: Your Vue app on another domain gets CORS errors, and a teammate wants to set allowed origins to '*'. Explain how CORS should be configured.

followUps.Laravel CORS Middleware and the fruitcak: How is CORS configured in Laravel, and why not use '*'?
followUps.Preflight Requests and OPTIONS Method Ha: What is a preflight request and what must the server answer?

evidence.text: CORS settings live in config/cors.php and are applied by middleware.
Allowed origins should list the exact frontend domains.
A wildcard cannot be used with credentials and would allow any site.
The browser sends an OPTIONS request first for non-simple requests.
The server must answer with CORS headers allowing the method and headers.
If the preflight fails, the real request is never sent.
